text:
Anita (Recruiting): Hey finance, my company card declined at SFO yesterday when I tried to grab a taxi to a candidate interview. I paid with my personal card and have the receipt but it shows USD + a separate 5% foreign transaction fee from my bank. Can I get reimbursed for both?
expense-bot: Reminder: Attach itemized merchant receipt and personal card statement showing the charge when submitting non-company card reimbursements.
Anita (Recruiting): attaching photo of the metered taxi receipt (shows fare $42.00) and a screenshot from my bank app showing conversion + fee: total charged $45.15 (includes $2.25 FX fee). No tip shown because I paid cash on pickup.
Elaine (Finance): Thanks Anita. For the reimbursement we need: 1) the taxi receipt, 2) the personal card statement line showing the $45.15 charge, and 3) a short note in the expense form explaining why the company card couldn't be used (e.g., "company card declined at terminal chip reader").
Anita (Recruiting): I added the note in the expense form and uploaded the two screenshots. Is the FX fee reimbursable?
Rafael (Finance Ops): Quick policy check: domestic taxi fares are reimbursable. Foreign transaction fees are handled case-by-case — usually we reimburse unavoidable bank fees if the employee had no other reasonable option and the spend was work-related. Since SFO is domestic, curious why there's an FX fee on Anita's CC. Did you use a foreign card?
Anita (Recruiting): oh — the personal card I used is a UK-issued card (I travel a lot), so my bank applied a cross-border fee even though transaction in USD. I can switch to my US card next time but needed the taxi in the moment.
Tom (Travel Admin): FYI we should check the company card tokenization with the airport providers — we've seen intermittent declines on chip readers. Filing a ticket with the card provider.
Elaine (Finance): For this claim: please upload a bank statement screenshot that shows the card issuer and the $45.15 posted transaction (we need proof of the FX fee line). Also Rafael, can you pre-approve a one-off for the FX fee if documentation looks good?
Rafael (Finance Ops): I can pre-approve up to $10 for foreign/bank fees for emergencies with manager signoff. Manager approving now please. @Tom could you confirm policy exception flow?
Tom (Travel Admin): Manager signoff required per policy 4.2. cc @Elaine — I can approve the exception if Anita confirms she tried company card and it declined. We also want a quick follow-up to Travel to avoid repeat.
Anita (Recruiting): Confirmed I tapped company card at SFO Terminal 2, got "card declined" on the reader. I have a photo of the terminal payment screen and the time. Uploaded to the expense.
Elaine (Finance): Received. Rafael, please mark this as "approved exception" in the expense system so Anita gets reimbursed for $45.15 (fare + FX). We'll code fare to RECRUIT-Q2 and the FX fee to "misc - bank fees". Anita, include tip amount if you tipped in cash later.
Rafael (Finance Ops): Marked approved. Expense status: Approved — awaiting payment. Case #FIN-2026-099.
Anita (Recruiting): Thanks all. One more Q: if this keeps happening and our corporate card can't be used, can recruiting carry a petty cash card?
Tom (Travel Admin): We prefer scope-limited virtual cards for teams with repeated problems. I'll run usage logs and if recruiting has >3 decline incidents in 30 days we'll recommend a virtual backup.
Elaine (Finance): Good plan. Also reminder to everyone: small bank fees under $10 may be reimbursed for exceptional circumstances but consistent foreign-card usage in the US should be handled by switching to a US-issued personal card or we can provision a team virtual.
Anita (Recruiting): noted, thanks. :pray:
expense-bot: Payment scheduled: EXP-2491 -> Anita (Personal Reimbursement) amount $45.15. ETA 5-7 biz days.
